methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Distalmotion is a Series G robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation framework draws on a comp universe of 10 same-sector peers—including one public company (277810.KQ) and nine private firms such as Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics—though none provided sufficient overlap at the same stage or valuation tier to support peer-median analysis.

Given the limited peer comparability at Series G, stage-progression methodology was applied as the primary triangulation approach. Using $150M in total raised as a proxy for cumulative company value and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G progression, this method yields an implied valuation of $188M. A sensitivity band around this point estimate—accounting for variance in step-up assumptions—produces a low case of $159M and a high case of $216M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $159M to $216M, centered on $188M. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable late-stage robotics companies in the data set, reliance on stage-progression rather than market-based peer multiples, and inability to cross-check against revenue, profitability, or growth metrics. A narrower range would require additional peer-level data or financial performance benchmarks specific to frontier manufacturing robotics at the Series G level.
